name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,323

entries.clue: Leaders of party in North Korea somewhat left-wing (4)

indicatorNotes.Leaders of: the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of Party, In, North, Korea

annotation.surface: A report on how far left the ruling party in North Korea sits.
annotation.walkthrough: Pink is a mild shade of red, so a pink politician leans left without being fully red.
annotation.definitionFit: A pale version of red, the colour of the left, so it marks mild socialist sympathies.

entries.clue: Verify odd bits of Rebus book (8)

indicatorNotes.odd bits of: the odd-numbered letters: first, third, fifth

blocks.note: to verify is to prove
R, B, S are letters 1, 3 and 5 of REBUS

annotation.surface: An instruction to check part of a Rebus novel, Ian Rankin's Edinburgh detective series.
annotation.walkthrough: Rebus looks like the detective or a picture puzzle, but it only lends its odd letters. The book is the Old Testament one.
annotation.definitionFit: Book here means one book of the Bible, the Old Testament collection of wise sayings attributed to Solomon.

entries.clue: Dig front of garden having bare border (5)

indicatorNotes.front of: the front of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.having: the border holds the letter inside it

blocks.note: nude = bare, split around the G
first letter of garden

annotation.surface: A gardener told to dig the front garden, which has a bare flower border.
annotation.walkthrough: Dig here is the noun, a dig in the ribs, not the spadework the garden suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: Dig as a noun is a poke with the elbow, the same gentle jab as prodding someone.

entries.clue: Furious old bird (8)

blocks.note: flaming = furious, in a flaming temper
O is the standard abbreviation for old

annotation.surface: An angry elderly bird, or an irate old woman.
annotation.walkthrough: Old bird reads as a single phrase for an elderly woman; split it and bird alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the long-legged pink wader of salt lagoons.

entries.clue: Tonight, I’ll be out covering Republican battleground in Montana (6,7)

indicatorNotes.out: the letters are put out of order
indicatorNotes.covering: the rearranged letters sit around the R

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
R = Republican, held inside the anagram

annotation.surface: Someone announcing a night out while a Republican faces a fight in Montana.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram of the first twelve letters wraps around R so the R lands in BIGHORN.
annotation.definitionFit: The Little Bighorn in Montana was the site of Custer's Last Stand in 1876.

entries.clue: Head of house of ill repute who can swing both ways (5)

annotation.definition: Head of house of ill repute

blocks.clueFragment: Head of house of ill repute
blocks.note: the woman who runs a brothel
a word that reads the same forwards and backwards

annotation.surface: A brothel keeper who is bisexual.
annotation.walkthrough: Swing both ways looks like a comment on her sex life; it means the word reads the same in either direction.
annotation.definitionFit: A madam is the woman in charge of a brothel, and MADAM is a palindrome.

entries.clue: Tory upset over article; party unable to comply (2,3,2)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down
indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, the first part sits above the next

blocks.note: Con = Conservative, the Tory party
an is the indefinite article
a do is a party

annotation.surface: A Conservative politician upset about a newspaper piece and a party that can't follow the rules.
annotation.walkthrough: Tory is a British Conservative; the abbreviation CON turned upside down gives NOC.
annotation.definitionFit: No can do is an informal way of saying you cannot comply.

entries.clue: Love New York Times material for cameo (4)

blocks.note: love = zero in tennis, O
standard abbreviation
X is the multiplication sign

annotation.surface: Someone who loves the New York Times and sees it as a place for a cameo appearance.
annotation.walkthrough: New York Times looks like one name, the newspaper; it splits into NY and X. A cameo is a carved stone brooch, not a brief film role.
annotation.definitionFit: Onyx, with its coloured layers, is a classic stone for carving cameos.

entries.clue: Ascot races hosting resistance leader from overseas (6)

indicatorNotes.races: the letters run about in a new order
indicatorNotes.hosting: the rearranged letters take R in as a guest

blocks.note: anagram fodder
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

annotation.surface: The Ascot horse races hosting a foreign resistance leader.
annotation.walkthrough: Ascot is an English racecourse, so races reads as the event itself rather than a sign to rearrange. Resistance leader also tempts, but R comes from resistance alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro led Cuba for decades.

entries.clue: Sailor that’s been in the cellar for ages? (3,4)

annotation.definition: Sailor that’s been in the cellar for ages?

blocks.note: the surface makes this a person; crosswords often use salt, tar or AB for one

blocks.clueFragment: that’s been in the cellar for ages?
blocks.note: a salt cellar holds table salt, so whatever has sat there for ages is aged seasoning

annotation.surface: A sailor who has been down in the cellar for years.
annotation.walkthrough: A salt cellar is the dish salt is kept in, so salt that has sat there for ages is old salt.
annotation.definitionFit: Salt is old slang for a sailor, and an aged one is a seasoned veteran of the sea.

entries.clue: Unreliable detective leading Yard (5)

indicatorNotes.leading: the detective comes before the Y

blocks.note: a dick is slang for a private detective
Y is the abbreviation for yard

annotation.surface: A dodgy detective heading up Scotland Yard.
annotation.walkthrough: Yard suggests Scotland Yard, London police headquarters, but here it is only the unit abbreviation. Dicky is British slang for shaky or unsound, as in a dicky heart.
annotation.definitionFit: A British informal adjective for something shaky or in poor condition, like a weak heart or a faulty engine.

entries.clue: Something happening? Still time (5)

blocks.note: even = still, as in even better
T is the abbreviation for time

annotation.surface: Someone asking whether anything is going on and hearing there's still time.
annotation.walkthrough: Still and even are both intensifiers: still better, even better.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an occurrence or incident, anything that takes place.

entries.clue: Keen American soldiers welcomed by lieutenant (6)

indicatorNotes.welcomed by: the lieutenant takes the soldiers inside

blocks.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, split around the rest
A = American
men = soldiers, as in officers and men

annotation.surface: Eager American troops greeted by their lieutenant.
annotation.walkthrough: Keen looks like an adjective meaning eager; here it is the verb, to wail in grief.
annotation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail for the dead, which is to lament.

entries.clue: Make a run for it carrying left over slice of meat (8)

indicatorNotes.carrying: the escape holds the other letters within it

blocks.note: to escape is to make a run for it; split around LO
L = left
O = over, the cricket abbreviation

annotation.surface: A thief bolting with the leftover meat.
annotation.walkthrough: Left over reads as leftovers but is two separate abbreviations. An over is a set of six balls in cricket.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a thin boneless cut, usually veal, beaten flat and fried.

entries.clue: BBC: No one cares about Welsh features (6,7)

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: The BBC complaining that nobody cares about its Welsh documentaries.
annotation.walkthrough: Features sounds like TV programmes but means landscape features. The Brecon Beacons are a mountain range in south Wales.
annotation.definitionFit: The Brecon Beacons are a range of hills, features of the Welsh landscape.

entries.clue: Heard rumours involving section of The Listener (7)

indicatorNotes.involving: the words contain the answer within them

blocks.note: hEARD RUMours

annotation.surface: Rumours overheard about part of The Listener, the old BBC magazine.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals make The Listener look like the BBC weekly; it is just someone listening, and the eardrum is part of them.
annotation.definitionFit: The eardrum is part of the ear, the listening organ.

entries.clue: Native Americans quickly besieging hotel (6)

blocks.note: apace = quickly, split around H
H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Native Americans rapidly surrounding a hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: Apache works as a plural as well as a singular, so it fits Native Americans.
annotation.definitionFit: The Apache are a group of Native American peoples of the Southwest.

entries.clue: Worship excludes American being nosy (6)

indicatorNotes.excludes: to exclude is to shut out, so the A is shut out of the word

blocks.note: praying = worship, in its -ing form
A = American, removed from PRAYING

annotation.surface: A comment that worship keeps out Americans who are nosy.
annotation.walkthrough: Worship has to be read as the verb form praying for the letters to work.
annotation.definitionFit: Prying means being nosy about others' affairs.

entries.clue: Best conceivable island trade (5)

blocks.note: I = island
to deal is to trade

annotation.surface: The finest possible trade deal for an island.
annotation.walkthrough: Best conceivable modifies the island trade in the surface, but it is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: perfect, as good as can be imagined.

entries.clue: Lost part of Great Seal (2,3)

indicatorNotes.part of: the answer is a part of the following words

blocks.note: greAT SEAl

annotation.surface: A missing piece of the Great Seal, the monarch's official stamp.
annotation.walkthrough: Lost looks like it describes a lost part of the seal; it is the definition, confused.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: sailors far from land are adrift, so the phrase came to mean confused or lost.

entries.clue: South Africa 55-0, lots of shots (5)

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
55 in Roman numerals
zero looks like the letter O

annotation.surface: A sports score: South Africa winning 55-0 after taking lots of shots.
annotation.walkthrough: The score line is the whole disguise: the numbers become Roman LV and the letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of many guns.

entries.clue: Cleaner vehicle transporting husband (4)

indicatorNotes.transporting: a vehicle transporting a passenger carries it inside, so H goes inside the car

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle, split around H
H = husband

annotation.surface: An eco-friendly car carrying someone's husband, or a cleaner driving him.
annotation.walkthrough: Cleaner looks like a comparative, a greener vehicle; it is the noun. A char, short for charwoman, is British for a cleaning lady.
annotation.definitionFit: A char is a woman employed to clean houses or offices.

entries.clue: Drug mule’s parent? (5)

blocks.note: street slang for heroin
a mule is a cross, bred from a donkey father and a mare mother

annotation.surface: Asking who the parent of a drug mule, a smuggler, might be.
annotation.walkthrough: Drug mule reads as one phrase, a courier of narcotics; split it and each half defines HORSE.
annotation.definitionFit: Horse is slang for heroin, and a mule's mother is a horse.

entries.clue: Tragedy returned to celebrity magazine (7)

indicatorNotes.returned: something returned is sent back, so its letters come back in reverse order

blocks.note: used as it stands, then turned back
Hello! is a British celebrity gossip magazine

annotation.surface: A tragic story sent back to a celebrity magazine.
annotation.walkthrough: To looks like a connecting word, but it is the letters reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Shakespeare's play about the jealous Moor of Venice is one of his tragedies.

entries.clue: Wandering little bird loses its heading (8)

indicatorNotes.loses its heading: the first letter is taken off

blocks.note: the brambling is a small finch; drop its B

annotation.surface: A small bird that has strayed and lost its sense of direction.
annotation.walkthrough: Heading looks like a compass direction for the wandering bird; it is the word's first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: straying aimlessly, whether on foot or in talk.

entries.clue: Flower emerged from bed (4)

blocks.note: the thorny garden bloom
got up in the morning: the past tense of rise

annotation.surface: A flower coming up out of a garden bed.
annotation.walkthrough: The bed looks like a flower bed; it is the one you sleep in.
annotation.definitionFit: A rose is a flower, and rose is the past tense of rise, to get up.
